title: Paper Radar Now Supports Claude Haiku for ArXiv Triage
summary: Paper Radar, the open-source ArXiv paper triage tool, now runs on Claude Haiku alongside existing models. Daily AI-powered research summaries at lower cost.
body_markdown:
#### 💡 TL;DR


- Paper Radar, an open-source ArXiv triage tool, now supports Claude Haiku for automated daily research paper summaries and filtering.
- The integration allows researchers to process academic papers at lower cost while maintaining quality, expanding model choice beyond existing options.
- Officially launched on November 12, 2026, the update is available on GitHub for immediate deployment by research teams and individual scientists.


Paper Radar, the open-source tool for automated ArXiv paper triage, now supports[Claude Haiku](https://emergent.sh/learn/what-is-claude-haiku-5-5) as a processing option. The update enables researchers to leverage Anthropic's fastest model for daily research paper summarization and filtering, adding a cost-effective alternative to existing model choices. Officially launched on November 12, 2026, the integration is available immediately through the project's GitHub repository.


## What Paper Radar Does


Paper Radar automates the daily workflow of scanning ArXiv, the preprint repository hosting over two million academic papers. The tool monitors new submissions, filters by research area or keyword, and generates structured summaries using large language models. Researchers configure their interests once, then receive daily digests of relevant papers without manual scanning.


The system processes paper abstracts, extracts key contributions, and ranks relevance based on user-defined criteria. Teams at universities and research labs use Paper Radar to stay current across rapidly moving fields like machine learning, quantum computing, and computational biology.


## Claude Haiku Integration Details


The new Claude Haiku support allows users to select Anthropic's efficient model as their processing backend. Claude Haiku offers faster inference times and lower token costs compared to larger models, making it practical for high-volume daily paper processing. According to the repository documentation, the integration maintains output quality while reducing computational overhead.


Users can switch between models through a configuration file, enabling A/B testing across different AI backends. The tool continues to support previously available models, giving research teams flexibility based on budget, speed, and accuracy requirements.


## Release Date and Availability


The Paper Radar update with Claude Haiku support officially launched on November 12, 2026. The source code is available under an open-source license on GitHub, allowing researchers to deploy the tool on their own infrastructure. Setup requires an Anthropic API key and basic Python environment configuration.


The project maintainer released installation scripts for Linux and macOS environments, with Windows support documented in the README. Community contributions have already added Docker deployment options and cloud function templates for serverless execution.


## Practical Applications


Research groups use Paper Radar to monitor niche subfields where a dozen relevant papers might appear weekly across thousands of daily ArXiv submissions. Graduate students configure the tool to track thesis-adjacent work, while principal investigators scan for collaboration opportunities and competitive research.


- Automated daily email digests with ranked paper summaries
- Customizable keyword and topic filters for precision targeting
- Multi-user support for research lab team deployments
- API integration for feeding curated papers into Slack or Notion


The addition of Claude Haiku makes these workflows more affordable for individual researchers and smaller labs operating on constrained budgets. Early adopters report processing costs dropping by approximately 60 percent compared to previous model choices while maintaining sufficient summarization accuracy.


## What This Means


The Paper Radar update reflects a broader trend of research tools expanding AI model support to balance cost and performance. As language models proliferate across speed and capability tiers, domain-specific applications gain flexibility to optimize for their exact use case. For academic researchers drowning in preprint volume, tools like Paper Radar with Claude Haiku support make it practical to maintain awareness without full-time literature review labor. The open-source nature ensures the research community can adapt the tool to emerging needs as both ArXiv submission rates and AI model capabilities continue to evolve.
